Use Tier 2: replace the current sampled-softmax training objective with BPR-max while retaining the existing GRU and causal attention architecture. The latest macro validation HR@10 of 0.5375 remains below the recorded best of 0.5400, so this experiment changes the ranking objective rather than tuning hyperparameters. Sampled softmax emphasizes identifying one positive among all sampled items; BPR-max instead concentrates learning on negatives the model currently scores highly. This could address insufficient separation around the top recommendation positions, although the reported metrics alone do not establish the cause of the plateau.

Focus on model_design and training_evaluation. Retain the existing 1,024 sampled negatives and training-history exclusion mask, but compute softmax weights over valid negative scores and minimize the negative logarithm of their weighted sigmoid positive-minus-negative margins. Add the standard BPR-max negative-score regularization term with coefficient 0.001, using numerically stable computations and excluding fully masked rows. Keep the architecture, sampling, optimizer, seeds, and training schedule unchanged to isolate this single objective replacement.

Select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 on the fixed 200 users and 99 unique negative candidates with evaluation seed 42, then report the four-category macro average. Preserve all dataset routing and ensure the predictor writer exports the same architecture and scoring forward pass used during validation, loading exactly one trained checkpoint per category. Keep the provided splits and DATA_DIR unchanged, write artifacts beneath the trial directory, and leave held-out prediction and evaluation to the host.
